findings.claim: The ticket makes a design choice with a rejected alternative (store images in OpenViking's native per-resource layout D/name/name instead of at the exact URI D/name through a temp folder and fs/mv, which spikes 3-5 showed leaves hidden folders), but no decision record holds it. CLAUDE.md requires one per choice. The component page states the layout but not why the exact-URI route was rejected, or that the operator accepted that markdown image links now point at a folder.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan says.
Images resolve to D/name/name and go up through temp_upload and an add resource with `to: D/name`.
Other non-UTF-8 objects are skipped with an INFO line.
Text still goes through content/write.
Deleting an image treats an empty `ls D/name` as gone.
Catch-up spares the old plain copy while its image is wanted.
Lock order holds and the tests check the eval rows' fails_when conditions.
The only finding is a missing decision record, which a plain fix covers, so the label is fix.
Gates: `loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree passed: pre_commit, cli_tests and eval rows r1-r6 all passed, stamp 4772618db8416571b23548c9d6ed3035de6e2390702206baf27c0cbc890e4a2c.
I also ran `just -f applications/ov-sync-consumer/justfile test` (vet plus the full module, ok) and test-one for each of the five named tests (ok).
Lock order: Apply takes the key, then Limit, the S3 read and tree.RLock.
upload makes all of its ls, delete, temp_upload and add calls under that RLock and takes no second key.
remove still takes RLock, releases it, then takes Lock, with no nesting.
Catch-up takes one key at a time, releases it, and calls Apply without holding a key.
Each OV request holds a MaxInFlight slot only for itself.
temp_upload goes through `call`, so it takes a slot and maps 409s.
Resolve's effect: a delete event for an image becomes remove(D/name/name).
removeIfEmpty(D/name, image=true) checks `ls D/name` after the recursive delete, then moves up to D, where the ghost folder stops the walk.
A replayed delete on a ghost or a missing folder ends cleanly.
Catch-up's want holds D/name/name and have gets it from Walk, while ghost folders are dirs and never count as files.
The old plain copy D/name: the want loop runs Apply first, which deletes it, and the guard keeps the stale have from removing it.
Once the image leaves the bucket, the guard no longer fires and catch-up removes the copy like any unwanted file.
An image at the mapped root works, since the loop covers root/name.png.
isImageHome: it needs an image extension, so no text path qualifies.
Old-sync text at X/y.png/y.png would only switch the folder check to the `ls D/name` form, which is harmless.
Git cannot hold a file and a folder with the same name, so image homes cannot collide with real paths.
Fake fidelity against spikes 1, 4, 6 and 8: `to` is the resource's own folder and a re-add replaces it (1).
Missing parents are created (4).
A recursive delete empties an image folder, but the folder stays in `ls D` as an isDir entry (6, 8).
A non-recursive delete of the folder gets 412 (8).
A content/write file reports isDir false (8).
The fake does not cover for the consumer: an add over a plain file at `to` leaves that file in place, so r2 would fail if the consumer skipped its delete.
Without the guard, the catch-up removal would get 412 and fail r5, which matches the builder's mutation claim.

Eval rows: r1 checks no content/write, the temp_upload bytes and filename, the add fields, call order, the stored bytes and unchanged siblings, plus case-insensitive extensions and errLockBusy through the add.
r2 checks that one non-recursive delete removes the plain copy, that a re-upload replaces the image with no further delete, and the exact contents of the folder.
r3 checks zero OV requests and one INFO line naming the key.
r4 checks no upload and content/write of multi-byte text byte for byte.
r5 checks present, missing, migrated and gone images, no forbidden deletes, no violations, a ghost folder that does not fail the pass, and an idempotent second pass.
r7 is an operator judgment for after release.
Errors: upload wraps delete and Upload errors with %w, call wraps errLockBusy, and remove wraps removeIfEmpty errors as errFolderLeft, so skipBusy and handle still sort them.
The add's `timeout: 120` is the same as Write's and stays under the 150 s client timeout in main.go.
Docs: I read the .okf component diff and found it accurate.
No docs/ page describes the byte handling.
f1 (docs, non-blocking): the native-layout choice and the exact-URI route it replaced need a decision record under `.okf/decisions/` (`kmctl new decision`).
Link it from the component page.
Catch-up re-runs Apply on every non-image binary every pass, because OpenViking never holds a copy of one.
Each run costs an S3 GET, a rate token and an INFO line.
The repo has no such file today (only the five PNGs fail UTF-8), so I am not raising it.
If an image leaves the bucket while its old plain copy is still at D/name, the event path runs `ls` on that plain file.
The fake answers 404.
The real server's answer was not measured.
The worst case is an errFolderLeft retry, and catch-up removes the copy anyway.
